i: The site is running out of stock on items, with the kitchen not flagging shortages until items are completely gone.
Stock communication is a front of house failure as much as a kitchen one, with the two teams not talking to each other.
The team is new and needs to master the basics of running the site: communication, sending staff on breaks at the right times and keeping stock consistent.
Negative reviews have increased, driven mainly by poor complaint handling.
Toilet maintenance issues, including broken holders and a blockage.
Ice supply is a gap until the new ice machine is installed, covered in the interim by a newly sourced supplier delivering weekly.
Too many managers were responding to the same issues during shifts, so a single point of contact was needed.
The site is exempt from KPI reporting until operations are fully established, so the focus is on operational basics rather than the KPI sheet.

Site conditions around waste management are messy, the area needs to be swept and disinfected, and two extra bins left on site are not needed, should be collected by the contractor and should not be used by staff.
Covers were down slightly while average spend increased, which the team attributed to the removal of the five pound ramen promotion.
Consistency in service and standards is vital to stop sales falling back, and the management team needs routines in place to avoid a chaotic environment.
Spend per head is low compared with brand standards and needs to be increased through active upselling.
Delegation of management duties lacks structure, with Spencer and Mia having no clear pattern to their weekly administration tasks, so daily and weekly tasks now need to be assigned properly.
Service standards have declined, with the site rating dropping over two weeks and a share of new reviews being negative, so leadership by example and constant communication are needed.

Labour is to be stabilised at its current level for the next three to four weeks without sacrificing service quality or food standards, and should not be reduced further, as maintaining service levels is critical during the first six to seven weeks of operation.

Stock take variance figures are inaccurate because invoices are missing and there is no daily routine for managing them, and only managers, not senior staff, should handle invoices so that there are no gaps when team members are on leave.
A kitchen allergy incident involving vegetable broth and a chicken ramen was raised, and allergen awareness training for the kitchen team is now a priority.
A video showing a mouse circulated publicly; the meeting concluded the impact had been minimal, but it sits alongside the site's other standards issues.
Covers fell on the week while spend per head rose, and sales came in ahead of target.

Deliveroo delivery management is a problem: an incorrect bag was handed out in a mix up and there is a run of missing item claims, so new protocols are being introduced to write the item count on the bag and photograph the packed food as evidence.
The site rating has slipped and management have set a daily Google review target to recover it; a realistic daily target was agreed in place of the much higher one that had been proposed.
Negative reviews concern staff, long waits, speed of service and loud music, so music will now be quieter and more relaxed through the day and upbeat at night.
Labour is high because of training hours for new starters and kitchen adjustments, and the rota will be trimmed with the area manager.
Staff turnover has come from letting people go and from delays in replacing them, compounded by absence and morale problems.
Covers and spend per head both rose week on week.
Sales were ahead of last week and ahead of target.
No intangibles audit was done this week.

The pass has worked very well from the front of house side, and delivery orders went out quickly and consistently.
Arguments in the kitchen were raised and have been addressed by the head chef, Roger.

Front of house needs to cut more labour than the kitchen, and Roger needs more guidance on cutting hours.
At the BOH meeting the agreed rota plan is to reduce weekday hours and move cover to weekend peaks; Srawut's review found the kitchen needs to save about £18 a day and FOH about £200 a day.
Sophie cautioned that labour cuts must not compromise food quality, complaints or allergy safety at a new site, and FOH needs time to train new staff after several leavers before hours are cut.
Site temporarily closed after a fire on Sunday night 11/10 in the back storage and kitchen area; no injuries; awaiting restoration. Sunday 11/10 not traded, so the week is six days.
Covers and spend per head down; only six days traded, heavy 5 GBP ramen voucher use, and new competitor Kibu opened three minutes away.
Sales target was raised this week, so the miss is wider; a normal Sunday (6,000 to 7,000 GBP) would have brought it close.

Labour poor: FOH cut well (9% Mon and Tue) but BOH stayed high.
